comments.body:
⚠️ severity: IMPORTANT —
⚠️ **IMPORTANT: the exported `effectiveVerdictOf` trusts every author when `logins` is absent — the `|| []` fail-closed default was dropped**

This helper is now part of `module.exports` (js/common/mergeVerdictGate.js:369), and at this line it parses with `{ authorLogins: inp.logins }` — no default. In `reviewVerdicts.authorAllowlist` a missing array (`authorLogins: undefined`) returns `null`, which means **no author filter at all**: every comment is trusted as a verdict record.

Contrast: the round-1 code called `parseVerdictRecords(comments, { authorLogins: inp.logins || [] })` — with `[]`, `collectAllowedRecords` filters every comment and trusts nothing. The module's documented doctrine (header + the `runGate` short-circuit comment: "No configured machine identity = nothing can ever be trusted") is fail-closed-on-trust for exactly this shape.

No current call path is affected — `runGate` short-circuits before this line when `logins` is empty, and `runGateForPr`/`machineLoginsOf` always produce a list — so this is not a behavior change. But the export makes the trust-everything default a supported entry point for the next caller: wiring the gate without a resolved `machineAuthor` would silently let a forged `REQUEST_CHANGES` marker hold merges (a merge-funnel DoS via fake verdict records). One-line fix restores the doctrine inside the helper:

```javascript
reviewVerdicts.parseVerdictRecords(comments,
    { authorLogins: inp.logins || [] }),
```

(Equivalently, guard at the top of `effectiveVerdictOf`.) A test pinning "direct call with no logins trusts nothing" would lock the doctrine in.
